explainer_reply:
Looking at the examples, I notice a strong recurring pattern: in nearly all high-activation examples, the highlighted tokens immediately follow a form of the verb "have":

- "have **no shame**", "has **26 home runs on**", "**had trouble holding back**", "I've **made comments about**", "has **some lively**", "have **been my ment**ors", "having **some manic episodes as**", "have **a mult**iline button", "have **had time to bring**", "has **passed would leave the**", "has **grown up around**", "had **some Wynd**ham", "Have **the following ingredients close**", "has **a comparative advantage in**"

Even in code, "HaveOcc**urred**" follows this pattern (the part after "Have"). The few exceptions (newlines, hyphens, "to eat") all have very low activation values, suggesting noise.

[EXPLANATION]: Text immediately following the verb "have" (including its forms has, had, having, and contractions like 've), i.e., the complement or object of the verb "have".
